trace.claim: Online political hostility is positively associated with indicators of political engagement and its antecedents, such as political interest, knowledge, and participation, and these hostile users are more active with greater potential reach.

{"text": "Existing explanations of online hostility can be grouped into at least two distinct literatures. One set of accounts emphasizes socioeconomic marginalization, status threat, and grievance. ... A second set of accounts emphasizes personality and ­emotion-regulation. ... In this article, we examine a different possibility. ... We extend this revisionist perspective to online political hostility by asking whether hostile political expression on X/Twitter is associated not only with deprivation or personality-based explanations, but also with political engagement and its antecedents.", "page": 2}
